question: If at same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is ₹44 and compound interest is ₹46, then what is the principal (in ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For 2 years, the ratio of CI to SI is given by: CI ÷ SI = 1 + (R ÷ 200)

⇒ 46 ÷ 44 = 1 + (R ÷ 200)

⇒ R ÷ 200 = (46 − 44) ÷ 44 = 2 ÷ 44 ⇒ R = 100/11 %

Now, Principal (P) = (SI × 100) ÷ (R × T)

⇒ P = (44 × 100) ÷ ((100/11) × 2) = (44 × 11) ÷ 2

**∴ The correct answer is ₹242.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) for 2 years = ₹44

Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years = ₹46

Time (T) = 2 years
